correctness.rationale: Counting maps from the n ballots onto j of k active labels yields the stated Stirling kernel; first-step conditioning gives the PGF. Each visited k has one geometric holding block with exit probability a_k at least ((k-1)/k)^n. At entry into {1,2}, the conditional ratio P(k,2)/P(k,1)=(k-1)(2^n-2)/2 gives the shortcut bound uniformly, and the post-entry time from 2 is an independent positive geometric. A deterministic shift u costs exactly 1-(1-q_n)^u in total variation, giving the displayed bound after averaging the entrance delay, including the empty delay for k=2. For fixed k, at first entry into {1,...,k}, the ratio of probabilities below and at k is O_k(((k-1)/k)^n) uniformly over the preceding state, by surjection count bounds. The resulting missing-visit probability changes h_k/a_k by O_k(1). The two-empty-bin term in a_k is O_k(((k-2)/k)^n); the reciprocal correction is bounded since k(k-2)/(k-1)^2<1 (and is zero at k=2). The tail above fixed r is bounded by the first remaining hold-time bound plus n times the next, giving the claimed exponential remainder. These analytic arguments do not rely on extrapolating the checker.
residual_risks: The hierarchy is for fixed r and the all-active start, not growing r or positive reinforcement. No formal proof certification or rerun of the supplied script.
